prompt: A resultant horizontal force of 65.0 N acts on a stationary block of mass 8.00 kg across a smooth horizontal floor over a distance of 12.0 m. Using the work-energy theorem, determine the final kinetic energy of the block.

mark_scheme.criterion: Applies the work-energy theorem: net work done W = F * s = Delta E_k.

hints: Recall the work-energy theorem: net work done equals the change in kinetic energy.
Because the block starts from rest, initial kinetic energy is zero.
solution:
By the work-energy theorem, net work done by the resultant force equals the change in kinetic energy:
W = Fs = Delta E_k = E_k,final - 0
E_k = 65.0 N * 12.0 m = 780 J.
teacher_walkthrough: Award C1 for equating work done by resultant force to kinetic energy gained: W = Fs = Delta E_k.
Point out that computing acceleration and final speed is unnecessary when applying work-energy directly.
